However, like many others, they struggle with the overwhelming patient numbers due to a shortage of GPs. While I've always spoken highly of them in the past, my recent experiences have been disappointing, particularly with some of the reception staff. The demeanour of some of the reception staff has become somewhat unpleasant, this week making me feel like an inconvenience when I visited to fill our a repeat prescription form and online registration.

Then today was a particular low point. After a busy morning getting my kids ready and off to school, I hurried home to contact the surgery about the same prescription request that had been questioned my my GP. The response I received was less than helpful—essentially telling me I should have called earlier at 8 am and that I'd need to wait until 1:30 pm now. There seemed to be no empathy or willingness to assist, trying to talk over me and leaving me feeling blamed for not navigating their inadequate process correctly.

While the practice itself is the best in the area, I believe there's a pressing need to address both the telephone manner and demeanour of some (though certainly not all) staff members. I hope they can improve in this area. Although I appreciate the challenges and stress it might cause for staff.. its also not the patients fault. Focus in this area would greatly enhance patient experience and restore the confidence I once had in them.

I look forward to calling at 130pm to be 17th person in the que, and no appointments left when I get to the front.

Edit: Another day - Another abrupt response from call handler that was totally unnecessary. Little empathy it seems for people in pain.  Inconveniencing them at there place of work when calling for help.  This used to be a very good surgery. Some training required here for staff, should be aware that sometimes people are in pain and that we should all be considerate to their needs.
